items.title: Free will: The real casualty of the algorithm
items.snippet: In the deserts of fourth-century Egypt, monks described a strange affliction: a restless urge to be anywhere but where they were, attending to any reality but the one in front of them. They called it acedia. Luke Burgis, author of Wanting: The Power of Mimetic Desire in Everyday Life , argues that our phones have made it socially contagious. items.title: Scientists discover a hidden reason why muscles weaken with age
items.snippet: Scientists have uncovered a hidden defense mechanism in aging muscles that sacrifices strength to protect cells from damage. In mice, partially restoring a crucial molecule reversed signs of muscle wasting and prevented premature death, raising hopes for new treatments for age-related muscle decline.
